statement: Discovery before writing code: arc-01 had already delivered the workpack's requested generic mechanisms (NdjsonWriter<T> as enforcer-core/src/ndjson_writer.rs, a SHA-256 hash-chain primitive as hash_chain.rs, two-layer redaction as redaction.rs) plus a mixed-record EnforcerEvent/RunEvent union in enforcer-domain/src/records.rs. d04's actual gap was narrower than the workpack text literally reads: a run-telemetry-SPECIFIC RunRecord DTO (schema_version, eventType, epochMs, command, ruleIdsInScope count, findings-by-severity, durationMs, exitStatus) and a run-telemetry sink wiring redaction+hash-chain+atomic-append together, writing to proof/telemetry/runs.ndjson.
why: Writing a duplicate ndjson.rs generic writer would have collided with arc-01's file and violated disjoint-file ownership; instead enforcer-core/src/telemetry.rs (new) rides the existing ndjson/hash_chain/redaction primitives rather than re-implementing them.
howToApply: Before implementing a workpack's stated files literally, grep the target crate's existing src/ tree for prior-landed mechanisms with the same name/purpose from earlier-numbered packs (arc-* usually lands first) -- the workpack prose can lag what's already been built.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-core/src/ndjson_writer.rs, hash_chain.rs, redaction.rs (pre-existing from arc-01); crates/enforcer-domain/src/records.rs (pre-existing from arc-02)

statement: Hash-chain tamper detection requires an independently-persisted digest, not a digest recomputed purely from the data file at verify time. First implementation of verify_file_chain recomputed digests from the NDJSON lines themselves and compared them to themselves -- this always 'verified' regardless of tampering, since there was no external record to diff against. Fixed by adding a parallel append-only '.chain' sidecar file (crates/enforcer-core/src/telemetry.rs: chain_sidecar_path, CHAIN_SIDECAR_SUFFIX) that RunTelemetrySink::append writes one recorded digest to per data line; verify_file_chain now reads both files and diffs recomputed-from-data against recorded-in-sidecar.
why: A caught-by-test design bug: the initial 'tampering_with_a_line_breaks_chain_verification' test failed because Ok(2) came back even after corrupting a line -- recomputation-only verification is not tamper-evident by construction.
howToApply: Any future hash-chain / tamper-evidence feature must persist the chain digests somewhere OTHER than a pure function of the file being protected (sidecar file, separate journal, or embedded-but-covering-different-bytes field) -- verifying a file's integrity by recomputing its own hash from itself and comparing to itself is a no-op check.

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-core --lib telemetry -- caught the bug: 'chain must break, got: Ok(2)' before the sidecar fix, all green after

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-core -p enforcer-domain; cargo clippy -p enforcer-domain -p enforcer-core --all-targets -- -D warnings

statement: d04 final gate: cargo build --workspace clean; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast (__COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker) shows only the same 2 pre-existing failures in enforcer-install (emitters::git_hooks::tests::each_flavor_writes_golden_bytes, emitters::consumer_ci::tests::apply_writes_exactly_the_five_workflow_files_with_golden_bytes) that d03's stream already documented as a pre-existing Windows CRLF/LF golden-byte artifact, reconfirmed present on baseline HEAD via git stash + re-run before this pack's changes. Every crate this pack touched (enforcer-core, enforcer-domain) is fully green. cargo fmt (workspace-wide) incidentally reformatted crates/enforcer-plan/tests/test_templates.rs (pre-existing file, not owned by d04) -- reverted that one file via git checkout to respect disjoint-file-ownership discipline before committing.
why: Documents both that d04 introduces zero regressions and that a workspace-wide `cargo fmt` run must be scoped back to only the files a lane owns before committing, since fmt has no file-list flag and will touch anything non-conformant workspace-wide.
howToApply: Future lanes: after running workspace-wide `cargo fmt`, run `git status --short` and `git checkout --` any file outside your owned-files list before staging/committing.

evidence.ref: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast; git status --short before/after git checkout -- crates/enforcer-plan/tests/test_templates.rs
